risks.note: Excess global LAB capacity from Middle East and Southeast Asian additions drove rising imports into India; domestic prices were supported only marginally by the anti-dumping duty on Qatari and Iranian LAB imposed for 5 years from June 23, 2025, and by mandatory BIS certification, so any lapse or circumvention of these measures reopens price pressure. Management also cited 'pricing pressures arising from unabated imports' as adversely impacting top-line performance.
risks.risk: Import competition and dependence on trade-remedy protection

risks.note: NP market availability contracted significantly while prices surged as most manufacturers relied on in-house NP production, creating a supply vacuum that the Company only mitigated by importing a substantial quantity in Q3. risks.risk: Raw material availability and price volatility (NP, benzene, crude linkage)

risks.note: Closure of the Strait of Hormuz following the Iran-Israel war disrupted imports and, via MoPNG sector-prioritisation directives, restricted the RLNG allocation from Indian Oil Corporation during March 2026 to 80% of the contracted quantum — a direct constraint on plant energy supply.

risks.note: The AR states that despite near-universal use of UOP technology, the cost of making LAB in India exceeds international standards due to the high cost of essential components such as energy and feedstock — a persistent margin disadvantage against imports. risks.risk: Structurally high Indian cost of production versus international benchmarks

risks.note: The LAB plant shutdown originally planned for 60 days was extended by nearly a month due to unforeseen execution delays, and the resulting lost production and sales fell below budgeted levels — evidence that turnaround slippage translates directly into volume loss.
risks.risk: Project execution risk on major revamps

risks.note: The domestic PO market faced significant challenges from the influx of lower-priced imported downstream polyols, making PO offtake a major challenge since Q3 of FY24-25, with recovery only anticipated from Q2 of FY 26-27.

currentContext.expansion: The planned capacity expansions in the Linear Alkyl Benzene plant and the Caustic Soda plant were completed during the last quarter of March 2026. The revamp of the LAB plant to enhance production capacity from 120 KTPA to 145 KTPA was successfully completed and commissioned in a safe manner on 11th March 2026; the shutdown originally planned for 60 days was extended by nearly a month due to unforeseen execution delays, with production commencing in the first week of March 2026. Adsorbent and associated hardware replacement carried out in the NP section of the LAB plant facilitated an increase in captive NP production to meet much of the intermediate required for the expanded LAB capacity. The Company also successfully completed the modernisation of the Caustic Soda plant, enhancing capacity from 150 TPD to 250 TPD, with the modernised plant enabling a reduction in specific power consumption for caustic soda lye production. Under its decarbonisation roadmap, the air preheater revamp and modification of the convection section of fired heaters to enhance heat recovery from flue gas have been completed, and installation of a waste heat recovery boiler to recover heat from gas engine exhaust has been completed and is on the verge of commissioning; detailed techno-commercial evaluations are in progress for the next viable initiatives. In BRSR Section A the Company reports 3 plants and 2 offices in India and no international operations.

- NP market availability contracted significantly while prices surged as most manufacturers relied on in-house NP production, creating a supply vacuum that the Company only mitigated by importing a substantial quantity in Q3. The Indian crude oil basket rose from a USD 63-70 per barrel range to USD 113.5 per barrel in March 2026, and NP and benzene consumption ran marginally above budget.
- Closure of the Strait of Hormuz following the Iran-Israel war disrupted imports and, via MoPNG sector-prioritisation directives, restricted the RLNG allocation from Indian Oil Corporation during March 2026 to 80% of the contracted quantum — a direct constraint on plant energy supply.
- The AR states that despite near-universal use of UOP technology, the cost of making LAB in India exceeds international standards due to the high cost of essential components such as energy and feedstock — a persistent margin disadvantage against imports. Power and fuel for LAB also ran above budget on unproductive consumption during the revamp shutdown and startup.
- The LAB plant shutdown originally planned for 60 days was extended by nearly a month due to unforeseen execution delays, and the resulting lost production and sales fell below budgeted levels — evidence that turnaround slippage translates directly into volume loss.
- The domestic PO market faced significant challenges from the influx of lower-priced imported downstream polyols, making PO offtake a major challenge since Q3 of FY24-25, with recovery only anticipated from Q2 of FY 26-27.
- New domestic capacities have raised production while national capacity utilisation of the roughly 6.4 million ton aggregate capacity is around 78%, and prices are still witnessing a declining trend; caustic soda output also depends on availability of sodium chloride, whose production fluctuations affect supply and pricing.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Prudent raw material sourcing and effective inventory management as a continued effort to sustain margins
- Cost optimisation, efficiency improvements and product mix enhancement alongside prudent financial management and a strong marketing strategy
- Debottlenecking and capacity expansion of the core LAB and Caustic Soda assets, with the LAB revamp (120 KTPA to 145 KTPA) and Caustic Soda modernisation (150 TPD to 250 TPD) completed in FY26

themes.title: Industrial gases, chlor-alkali & commodity chemicals
themes.need: A capacity-led commodity-chemical and industrial-gas cycle underpins the basic-materials chain - ELLEN on air-separation/industrial gases; EPIGRAL/CHEMPLASTS/DCW/DCMSHRIRAM/GHCL/TATACHEM/GNFC on chlor-alkali, soda-ash and vinyls; LORDSCHLO on caustic; CHEMBONDCH on water-treatment chemicals. Pricing/utilization and energy costs are the near-term swing factors.
themes.driver: Caustic/soda-ash price recovery; utilization ramp on new capacity; energy-cost relief.
